amendments.because: Owner: every feature is proven for new and existing clients
amendments.done_when: A 'forge fasttest <base>' command works in any pytest repo without installing Forge into the project: Forge picks the changed test files, test files named after a changed module, and test files importing or mentioning it, then runs the repo's own test command from forge.toml narrowed to those files in the repo's environment, runs the full test command when conftest.py, pyproject.toml or a lock file changed, and caps pytest at half the machine's cores; no pytest plugin. Forge's own forge.toml and the skill use 'forge fasttest {base}'; doctor reports a fast_test that still says 'python -m forge.fasttest' with the one-line replacement. New repos: setup proposes it for pytest repos. Existing repos: get the command on upgrade; their forge.toml is never rewritten. One command-level test in a plain pytest repo without Forge installed in its environment.

Forge's own forge.toml and the skill use 'forge fasttest {base}'; doctor reports a fast_test that still says 'python -m forge.fasttest' with the one-line replacement. Command-level tests cover both kinds of client: a new client (forge init in a plain pytest repo, Forge not installed in its environment) whose proposed fast_test runs only the related tests at close; and an existing client adopted on an earlier release whose forge.toml carries the old 'python -m forge.fasttest' line, where doctor names the replacement, forge.toml is not rewritten, and after the owner's one-line change close runs only the related tests.

findings.body: The previously reported defect remains: `python -m pip install pytest && python -m pytest tests` matches both `pytest` tokens and receives picker arguments on the pip invocation, causing setup to fail. The fallback at line 81 also appends pytest arguments to Ruff in `python run_tests.py && ruff check .`, even when the launcher forwards arguments as required by the ruling. Locate the actual pytest invocation or launcher and preserve the other shell commands.
findings.title: Recognize pytest invocations before adding pytest arguments

findings.body: The previously reported defect remains: this loop combines every configuration candidate, including defaults when `-c` selects another file. With an active pytest.ini containing no xdist options and an inactive tox.ini containing `addopts = -n auto`, Forge injects `--maxprocesses` into a valid command; without xdist installed, pytest rejects it. [Pytest selects one configuration file and never merges candidates](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/reference/customize.html). Inspect only the configuration selected for that invocation.
findings.title: Read worker options only from pytest's selected configuration

findings.body: The previously reported defect remains: explicit unrelated targets are removed only from the command string. `tests/test_unrelated.py::test_unrelated` in configuration addopts or PYTEST_ADDOPTS survives the appended ignore arguments. [Pytest bypasses ignore checks for explicitly supplied files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytest-dev/pytest/9.1.1/src/_pytest/main.py), so unrelated tests still run despite the printed selection. Filter explicit excluded targets from both option sources while preserving their other settings.
findings.title: Exclude unrelated paths supplied through pytest addopts

findings.body: Whenever unrelated files exist, the picker now passes `@selection.txt` to the client's pytest. [Argument-file support was introduced in pytest 8.2](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/usage.html#read-arguments-from-file). A client pinned to pytest 7.x or 8.1 therefore interprets this as a collection path and exits with a file-not-found error instead of running related tests. Preserve a narrowing path supported by those versions; the new tests exercise only the repository's installed pytest.
findings.title: Support pytest versions before 8.2 when narrowing tests

findings.body: The previously reported contradiction remains. Immediately after advertising the external picker, line 302 instructs agents to use “the repo's Python runner with Forge installed.” The same instruction appears at line 302 in both .codex/skills/forge/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/forge/SKILL.md. This can direct new clients to install Forge into their project unnecessarily. Clarify that the project runner belongs in `test`, while the separately installed Forge tool runs the picker.
findings.title: Remove the project-install instruction from setup guidance

why: The shipped Python test picker (uv run python -m forge.fasttest) fails in client repos with 'No module named forge', because Forge is a separate tool, not a dependency of the client's project; it only works in Forge's own repo
